- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.1) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward → reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots → cap forecast at 1–2% below peak or adjust downward by 3–5 days.
- If sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg 0–0.1), model frequently overestimates mean → shift forecast mean down by 1–3% relative to recent 10-day average.
- Model underestimates true price when sentiment is negative and price is trending down → add 1–2% to forecast for 3–5 days ahead.
- Forecast horizon > 14 days shows persistent lag → adjust for 1–2% downward bias per 7-day interval beyond 14 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., +0.3 → -0.4 → +0.1), model fails to capture mean reversion → apply 1–3% downward correction at 7–10 day mark.
